v1.0.0.changelog: Initial model training and local inference pipeline deployment.

spec.overview: An edge-deployed machine learning system performing real-time anomaly detection and predictive maintenance on motor vibration and temperature sensors.
spec.architecture: Utilizes a Python-based preprocessing and feature engineering pipeline, classical ML classifiers trained offline, and lightweight local inference engines deployed without cloud reliance.

subsystems.name: Frontend Dashboard
subsystems.function: Visualizes real-time sensor metrics and alert signals.

subsystems.name: Telemetry API
subsystems.function: Exposes FAST REST endpoints for raw vibration feeds.

subsystems.name: Data Engine
subsystems.function: Buffers sensor logs locally in sliding windows.

subsystems.name: Inference Core
subsystems.function: Predicts equipment failures with Random Forest classifiers.

subsystems.name: Edge Node
subsystems.function: Local inference loops running offline on target boards.

spec.challenges: Faced severe memory and processor limits when attempting to compute FFT frequency conversions on local edge microcontrollers.
spec.engineeringDecisions: Shifted anomaly features from frequency domains to time domains (root-mean-square and peak-to-peak amplitude metrics), achieving 88% precision with a 90% reduction in CPU cycles.
spec.lessonsLearned: Offline model training must replicate the specific coordinate limits and noise characteristics of real-world physical sensors.
spec.futureImprovements: Port model weights into C headers using micro-tensor toolkits to support ultra-low-power microcontrollers.

interviewQuestions.q: Why did you choose classical ML over Deep Learning (like LSTM) for anomaly detection?
interviewQuestions.a: Deep learning models require high memory capacities and floating-point acceleration. Classical Random Forest models achieved 88% precision while using less than 50KB of memory, which fits directly on edge microcontrollers without network delays.

replay.title: Feature Engineering Core
replay.description: Engineered statistical time-domain features (RMS, Peak-to-Peak) from sensor inputs.
replay.decisions: Substituted heavy FFT transformations with time-series statistics to fit hardware microcontrollers.
replay.challenges: Extremely low processing capabilities of the target board.
replay.lessons: Pre-aggregating sensor windows offsets raw parsing latency.

replay.title: Model Training & Evaluation
replay.description: Trained classical Random Forest estimators, benchmarking against linear SVM models.
replay.decisions: Used synthetic oversampling (SMOTE) to balance the minority anomaly class (2% of samples).
replay.challenges: Extreme class imbalance led to high false-negative rates initially.
replay.lessons: Tuning classification decision thresholds is more critical than maximizing overall accuracy.

replay.title: Edge Inference Deployment
replay.description: Ported Python model parameters into optimized matrix multiplication steps running directly on the sensor board.
replay.decisions: Avoided cloud roundtrips by compiling classification logic to run in local edge loops.
replay.challenges: Float division operations caused performance lags on edge hardware.
replay.lessons: Scaling weights to integer categories allows microcontrollers to run inference in sub-millisecond ranges.
